questions.q: If the length of the minor axis of an ellipse is equal to one fourth of the distance between the foci, then the eccentricity of the ellipse is :

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Product of focal distances }=\left(a+e x_1\right)\left(a-e x_1\right) \\ & =a^2-e^2 x_1^2=a^2-e^2(3) \\ & =a^2-3 e^2=\frac{7}{4} \Rightarrow a^2=\frac{7}{4}+3 e^2 \\ & \Rightarrow 4 a^2=7+12 e^2 \\ & \&\left(\sqrt{3}, \frac{1}{2}\right) \text { lines on } \frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1 \\ & \therefore \frac{3}{a^2}+\frac{1}{4 b^2}=1\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \frac{3}{\mathrm{a}^2}+\frac{1}{4\left(\mathrm{a}^2\right)\left(1-\mathrm{e}^2\right)}=1 \\ & 12\left(1-\mathrm{e}^2\right)+1=4 \mathrm{a}^2\left(1-\mathrm{e}^2\right) \\ & 13-12 \mathrm{e}^2=\left(7+12 \mathrm{e}^2\right)\left(1-\mathrm{e}^2\right) \\ & \Rightarrow 13-12 \mathrm{e}^2=7-7 \mathrm{e}^2+12 \mathrm{e}^2-12 \mathrm{e}^4 \\ & \Rightarrow 12 \mathrm{e}^4-17 \mathrm{e}^2+6=0 \\ & \therefore \mathrm{e}^2=\frac{17 \pm \sqrt{289-288}}{24}=\frac{17 \pm 1}{24}=\frac{3}{4} \& \frac{2}{3} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{e}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \& \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}} \\ & \therefore \text { difference }==\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}=\frac{3-2 \sqrt{2}}{2 \sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>:</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>a</mi><mo>></mo><mi>b</mi><mo>.</mo></math> Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> be another ellipse such that it touches the end points of major axis of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and the foci of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> are the end points of minor axis of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>.</mo></math> If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>E</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> have same eccentricities, then its value is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given ellipse is E1:x2a2+y2b2=1, a>b and E2 is another ellipse which touches the end points of the major axis of E1 and foci of E2 are at the minor axis of E1, thus the two ellipses are given by the following diagram.

Since, the ellipse E2 touches the major axis of the ellipse E1, hence, the minor axis of the ellipse E2 is a1=a.

Now, let the major axis of the ellipse E2 is b1=c and it is obvious from the diagram and the given conditions that b1>a1.

We know that the eccentricity of an ellipse x2A2+y2B2=1, A>B is 1-B2A2.

Thus, for the ellipse E1, we have e=1-b2a2 and for the ellipse E2, we have e1=1-a2c2.

Given, e=e1

1-b2a2=1-a2c2

⇒ 1-b2a2=1-a2c2

⇒ b2a2=a2c2

⇒ c2=a4b2

⇒ c=a2b   ...i

Also, given that the foci of E2 are the end points of the minor axis of E1, thus b=ce

⇒ c=be   ...ii

From the above two equations, we get be=a2 b

⇒ e=b2a2

Now, using the definition of eccentricity, we get e=b2a2=1-e2

⇒ e2+e-1=0

Now, applying the Sridharacharya's formula for the roots of a quadratic equation, i.e. if ax2+bx+c=0, a≠0, then x=-b±b2-4ac2a, we get

e=-1±12-4×1×-12×1

⇒ e=-1±1+42

⇒ e=-1±52

But, eccentricity can never be negative, hence e=-1+52.

$A=\{(\alpha, \beta) \in \mathbf{R} \times \mathbf{R}:|\alpha-1| \leq 4 \text { and }|\beta-5| \leq 6\}$
and
$B=\left\{(\alpha, \beta) \in \mathbf{R} \times \mathbf{R}: 16(\alpha-2)^2+9(\beta-6)^2 \leq 144\right\}$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text { A : }|x-1| \leq 4 \text { and }|y-5| \leq 6 \\ & \Rightarrow-4 \leq x-1 \leq 4 \Rightarrow-6 \leq y-5 \leq 6 \\ & \Rightarrow-3 \leq x \leq 5 \quad \Rightarrow-1 \leq y \leq 11 \\ & \text { B : } 16(x-2)^2+9(y-6)^2 \leq 144 \\ & \text { B : } \frac{(x-2)^2}{9}+\frac{(y-6)^2}{16} \leq 1\end{aligned}$

From Diagram $\mathrm{B} \subset \mathrm{A}$

If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Δ</mi><msup><mi>S</mi><mo>'</mo></msup><mi>B</mi><mi>S</mi></math> is a right angled triangle with right angle at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> and area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>Δ</mi><msup><mi>S</mi><mo>'</mo></msup><mi>B</mi><mi>S</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi>sq</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>units</mi></math>, then the length of a latus rectum of the ellipse is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given that, 

∠SBS'=π2

⇒∠OBS=π4

⇒b=ae  ...i 

Also, area ∆SBS'=8 

⇒12.2ae.b=8

⇒aeb=8  ...ii 

From equations i & ii, 

b2=8 and a2=b2+a2e2=8+8=16

⇒b=22 and a=4

Thus, the length of the latus rectum is 2b2a=164=4

questions.q: Let $C$ be the circle of minimum area enclosing the ellipse $E: \frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ with eccentricity $\frac{1}{2}$ and foci $( \pm 2,0)$. Let PQR be a variable triangle, whose vertex $P$ is on the circle $C$ and the side $Q R$ of length 29 is parallel to the major axis of $E$ and contains the point of intersection of $E$ with the negative $y$-axis. Then the maximum area of the triangle PQR is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Area of $\triangle P Q R$
$\begin{aligned}
& =\frac{1}{2}(2 a)(a \sin \theta+b) \\ & \therefore \text { maximum area }=a(a+b) \\ & \quad=4(4+2 \sqrt{3})=8(2+\sqrt{3})
\end{aligned}$
